request.spec:
Show the duplicate claims: for each person, date and amount with two or more claims (VOID and
DELETED claims left out), one line <name> <date> <amount> x<count>, people in list order, then by
date, then by amount.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show the duplicate claims: for each person, date and amount with two or more claims (VOID and
DELETED claims left out), one line <name> <date> <amount> x<count>, people in list order, then by
date, then by amount.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The duplicate-claims list now works, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec: the new duplicate-claims test and the three existing scenarios.

A new "Duplicate claims" panel on the sheet has a **Show** button. Pressing it lists one line per person, date and amount that has two or more claims, as `<name> <date> <amount> x<count>`. VOID and DELETED claims are left out, and lines are ordered by people in list order, then by date, then by amount. It only reads data, so it writes nothing to the store or the audit file.

**Server:** a new endpoint, `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/duplicates`, set up in `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/duplicates.GET.yml`. The logic is in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/claim/RespondWithDuplicates.java` and uses the existing `People` and `Claims` lookups.

**Front end:** `src/main/frontend/features/duplicates/duplicates.slot.tsx` adds the panel, following the pattern of the existing Activity panel. It has the `dups-show` button the test presses and one `dup-line` element per result. Pressing Show again clears the old lines before the new ones load, so two presses can be told apart. If the request fails, it shows a `dups-error` message.

No database changes were needed.
